result.topic_en: Gauss notes that the backward-extended arithmetic-geometric mean sequence b tends to 0 while a grows without bound, and gives a numerical example of the forward and backward AGM sequences for a = 1, b = 0.2.

methods.what: Backward extension of the AGM: the product of the preceding pair equals the square of b (inverse AGM step)
Numerical table of the AGM sequences extended forward and backward for a=1, b=0.2, converging to 0.5208016382
Conclusion that the backward b-sequence tends to zero

items.english: In order to see clearly how quickly such series II approach their limits from both sides, and I from the right, and how I goes beyond all bounds from the left, some examples are set down here.
